Just weeks after announcing a price hike for Apple Music, Apple today announced that Apple TV+ will also be getting a price increase. Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that Apple TV+ will rise from $12.99 to $14.99 per month.

The Apple One Individual plan will also see its monthly fee raised.

Apple TV+ and Apple One price increases

Here are the full details of this price hike:

  • Apple TV+ (monthly): $14.99 (previously $12.99)
  • Apple TV+ (annual): $119 (previously $99)
  • Apple One Individual: $21.95 (previously $19.95)

Pricing for the other Apple One plans remains unchanged. When Apple raised Apple Music prices last month, it also raised the monthly fees for the Apple One Family and Apple One Premier plans, but left the Individual plan unchanged.

The new pricing takes effect immediately for new subscribers. Apple says existing subscribers will receive a notification about the price increase roughly a month before being charged the new rate.

The last time Apple raised the monthly fee for Apple TV+ was in August 2025, when it went from $9.99 to $12.99 per month. At that time, Apple did not adjust the annual plan pricing or the Apple One bundles.

Apple has significantly expanded the Apple TV+ content lineup over the past year. Last October, Apple announced a deal making it the exclusive U.S. broadcast partner for F1 (Formula 1). The F1 streaming service is included with a standard Apple TV+ subscription at no extra cost.

Earlier this year, Apple also added MLS (Major League Soccer) streaming to Apple TV+, again at no extra cost. Previously, watching MLS required a separate MLS Season Pass subscription.

Apple is also riding the momentum of several recent hit shows, such as the fourth season of Ted Lasso. Today, Apple TV+ is also premiering the second season of Dark Matter. The sixth season of Slow Horses will debut on September 16.

What do you think of the new Apple TV+ pricing? Is $14.99 per month worth it for the Apple TV+ content lineup? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.
